newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two French soldiers killed by ageing Verdun shell.
newsitem.headline: Two French soldiers killed by ageing Verdun shell.

text.p: Two French soldiers died on Sunday when a shell from the First World War exploded on the 1916 battlefield of Verdun, paramilitary gendarmes said.

The two non-commissioned officers from a helicopter regiment based nearby at Etain-Rouvres, were walking in a so-called "red zone" of the countryside away from recommended paths when the shell exploded.
"We don't know exactly what happened. At this time of year shells are sometimes pushed to the surface with the repeated frosts and thaws. Maybe they stepped on it," a gendarme said.

About 350,000 people died in the 10-month battle of Verdun, which began when German forces launched an assault to break through French lines to capture Paris. The deadlocked battle and its carnage became a symbol of the futility of war.
Many areas of northern France are still dangerous because of rusting shells from the 1914-18 war.
